stances.claim: The Framework Agreement is vague in places but not yet unconstitutional because it is a work in progress -- not self-executory, not the source of specifically enforceable rights -- and charges of unconstitutionality are premature and at best speculative.
stances.confidence: asserted with in my humble view

stances.claim: The ministerial form of government for Bangsamoro is constitutionally permissible: the Constitution mandates a presidential system only at the national level and does not bar a ministerial form at the regional level.

Unlike the MOA-AD which created a separate state (struck down in North Cotabato), the Framework Agreement explicitly recognizes the overarching power of Philippine laws and institutions -- making the prior MOA-AD ruling inapplicable.
stances.rhetorical_move: MOA-AD-distinction as the key constitutional safe harbor

stances.claim: The real constitutional tests will come with the four annexes, the final peace agreement, and the Bangsamoro Basic Law -- not the Framework Agreement itself, which is merely a road map.

notable_anecdotes: Aquino describing ARMM as a failed experiment -- the most politically pointed phrase in the column, coming from the president replacing it.
CJ description of Leonen required skills: His tiptoeing skills will all the more be needed in negotiating these sensitive documents -- the most vivid image of the delicacy of the negotiations ahead.

The North Cotabato v. Government precedent as the lesson the Leonen-Iqbal team was keenly aware of -- showing how the struck-down MOA-AD ghost shaped the Framework Agreement careful avoidance of separate-state language.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban assesses the Bangsamoro Framework Agreement between the Philippine government and the MILF as 'a modest but essential beginning, a road map to a shared vision of peace' -- vague in places but not yet unconstitutional. Bangsamoro will replace ARMM (which Aquino described as a 'failed experiment') as a new political unit with a ministerial form of government, a new layer of governance to which local government units will report, with constitutive LGUs given a plebiscite vote on inclusion. Most Framework Agreement provisions are not self-executory and not yet sources of specifically enforceable rights -- charges of unconstitutionality are 'premature and at best speculative.' The ministerial form is constitutionally permissible: the Constitution mandates a presidential system only at the national level, and the autonomous region organic act need only define an elective executive department and legislative assembly, not prohibiting a ministerial structure. He distinguishes the Framework Agreement from the struck-down MOA-AD (North Cotabato v. Government, October 14, 2008, J. Carpio Morales): the MOA-AD created a separate state; the Framework Agreement explicitly recognizes the overarching power of Philippine laws and institutions, the national COA's full audit authority, and constitutional supremacy. The real constitutional tests will come with the four annexes, the final peace agreement, and the Bangsamoro Basic Law Congress must enact -- where chief negotiator Marvic Leonen's 'tiptoeing skills will all the more be needed.'
